root_cause.text: The hardware's automatic chip select (CS) control, which asserts the built-in CS whenever data is written and deasserts it after the configured transfer length, interferes with GPIO-based CS lines when multiple devices are present, causing unintended activation of the built-in CS during accesses to other devices.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "It was reported to me that if there are two devices attached to this QSPI controller that the in-built chip select is set low while linux tries to access the device attached to the GPIO." The patch disables automatic CS and adds software control via the DIRECT_ACCESS register (DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL bit) and implements `mchp_coreqspi_set_cs` to manually manage the built-in CS.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add QSPI Direct Access register bit definitions to enable upcoming direct access mode support.
intent_record.what: Added three new preprocessor constants: DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL (BIT(0)), DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL (BIT(1)), and DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL_SHIFT (1), along with a comment block describing them as QSPI Direct Access register defines.
intent_record.how: These defines make the bit positions available for use in driver code to manipulate the QSPI Direct Access register, enabling future implementation of direct access mode operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add spi_set_cs and spi_setup callbacks to correctly initialize and control chip select polarity for active-low devices.
intent_record.what: Added two static functions: mchp_coreqspi_set_cs to control chip select line state via DIRECT_ACCESS register, and mchp_coreqspi_setup to set the chip select to its inactive state during probe for devices with active-low polarity.
intent_record.how: The set_cs function reads the REG_DIRECT_ACCESS register, clears the chip select bits, and sets them based on enable (inverted). The setup function, for devices without SPI_CS_HIGH, sets the chip select bits to ensure inactive (high) state. This implements proper chip select handling and initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Delete unused mchp_coreqspi_setup_op function to clean up the driver code.
intent_record.what: Removed the static function mchp_coreqspi_setup_op which was setting CONTROL_MASTER, CONTROL_ENABLE, and clearing CONTROL_CLKIDLE in the control register.
intent_record.how: The function is no longer present in the driver, eliminating any calls to it. If it was dead code, no runtime change; otherwise, its register setup must be performed elsewhere or is no longer necessary.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add explicit chip select assertion before SPI memory operation to ensure proper slave selection.
intent_record.what: Added a call to mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, true) after mchp_coreqspi_config_op and before the opcode check in mchp_coreqspi_exec_op.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the chip select line is asserted (true) before starting any SPI memory operation, preventing communication failures due to missing or incorrect slave selection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add chip select deassertion in error path to ensure proper cleanup after SPI operation failure.
intent_record.what: Added a call to mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, false) at the error label in mchp_coreqspi_exec_op.
intent_record.how: On error (e.g., timeout), the chip select is now deasserted before releasing the op_lock and disabling interrupts, preventing the SPI device from being left with CS asserted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add variable declarations for chip select count and a generic value to support upcoming device tree property parsing in the SPI controller probe function.
intent_record.what: Added declarations for two unsigned 32-bit integer variables `num_cs` and `val` at the beginning of `mchp_coreqspi_probe`, after the existing `int ret;` declaration.
intent_record.how: The change introduces variables that are not yet used in the shown context; their presence prepares for future code (e.g., reading device tree properties) but does not alter current runtime behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SPI controller probe to properly configure chip select count and remove unused custom setup callback.
intent_record.what: Added reading of 'num-cs' device tree property to set number of chip selects (default 1) and removed the assignment of a custom setup callback (ctlr->setup = mchp_coreqspi_setup_op).
intent_record.how: The driver now explicitly sets ctlr->num_chipselect based on the device tree or defaults to 1, and no longer overrides the default SPI setup behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix chip select handling by replacing static chip select count with custom callbacks and ensuring hardware is configured for software-controlled chip select enable.
intent_record.what: Removed the line setting ctlr->num_chipselect to 2; added assignment of ctlr->setup and ctlr->set_cs function pointers; added code to enable the controller in master mode and set the direct access register to enable software-controlled chip select.
intent_record.how: The driver no longer specifies a fixed number of chip selects, instead relying on the SPI core's default or GPIO descriptors. It now provides custom setup and chip select control callbacks, and explicitly initializes the hardware to operate in master mode and with software-controlled chip selects, enabling flexible CS management.

The group directly mitigates the automatic chip select interference by replacing static chip select handling with custom callbacks and configuring hardware for software-controlled chip select, which is exactly the fix for the vulnerability root cause.
The group adds explicit chip select assertion to mitigate the interference caused by hardware automatic CS, directly addressing the root cause.

The error path chip select deassertion directly addresses proper CS line management, which is central to the vulnerability involving interference between hardware automatic CS and GPIO-based CS. Ensuring cleanup on failure prevents unintended CS states that could exacerbate the root cause.

The added variables for chip select count and generic value are preparatory steps for parsing device tree properties, which are necessary to configure and manage multiple chip select lines, directly addressing the root cause of CS interference.

candidates.rationale: Setting a static chip select count implies use of hardware automatic CS control, which interferes with GPIO CS lines when multiple devices are present. The fix replaces this with dynamic configuration and custom callbacks.
This custom setup callback likely configured hardware automatic CS behavior without disabling it for GPIO-controlled CS lines, causing unintended CS activation.

This function configures the operation including transfer length, which triggers hardware automatic CS assertion/deassertion; the lack of explicit CS control before this call leads to interference with GPIO CS.
Enabling GPIO descriptors without disabling hardware automatic CS causes the built-in CS to fire during accesses to other devices, as the hardware CS is not properly overridden.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces regular transfer support via mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one and mchp_coreqspi_prepare_message. In prepare_message, the frame length is configured (REG_FRAMESUP and REG_FRAMES) and control bits are set that cause the hardware to automatically assert its built-in chip select during data writes. There is no code to disable this hardware CS when GPIO-based CS is used, so the vulnerable construct (automatic hardware CS interfering with GPIO CS) is present and unfixed.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds support for regular transfers and enables GPIO chip select descriptors (ctlr->use_gpio_descriptors = true, ctlr->num_chipselect = 2). However, in mchp_coreqspi_prepare_message, the hardware's automatic chip select is still configured by writing total_bytes to REG_FRAMES (via frames = total_bytes & BYTESUPPER_MASK; writel_relaxed(frames, qspi->regs + REG_FRAMESUP); and writel_relaxed(frames, qspi->regs + REG_FRAMES)). This means the hardware will assert its built-in CS for the entire transfer length, even when a GPIO CS line is used. This interference is exactly the vulnerability described: the hardware's automatic CS control interferes with GPIO-based CS lines when multiple devices are present. No mechanism to disable hardware CS when GPIO CS is active is present in this commit.

Author: Naga Sureshkumar Relli <nagasuresh.relli@microchip.com>

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add support for microchip fpga qspi controllers
    
    Add a driver for Microchip FPGA QSPI controllers. This driver also
    supports "hard" QSPI controllers on Polarfire SoC.
    
    Signed-off-by: Naga Sureshkumar Relli <nagasuresh.relli@microchip.com>
    Reviewed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The driver initializes the hardware with `CONTROL_MASTER | CONTROL_ENABLE` in `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op` (line 255), enabling the hardware's automatic chip select control. There is no logic to manage CS lines when multiple devices are present (e.g., no GPIO CS handling, no per-transfer CS toggling, and no disabling of automatic CS). The hardware's automatic CS will assert on every data write and deassert after the configured transfer length, which can interfere with GPIO-based CS lines on other devices, matching the described vulnerability. This initial commit introduces the driver without any such mitigation, so the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The driver code does not explicitly disable the hardware's automatic chip select control. In the setup function (mchp_coreqspi_setup_op), only CONTROL_MASTER and CONTROL_ENABLE are set, with no bit to disable automatic CS. The exec_op function (mchp_coreqspi_exec_op) configures frames but does not touch any CS control register. This absence allows the hardware's automatic CS to interfere with GPIO-based CS lines when multiple devices are used, matching the vulnerability root cause. Since this is the initial commit, no fix is present.
